challenges.title: Ramadan, the overtime cap and WPS deadlines

items.title: Shortened Ramadan hours for everyone
items.text: During the holy month of Ramadan, regular daily working hours are cut by 2 hours — with no reduction in pay, for every private-sector employee regardless of religion (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, Art. 17, read with Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022).

items.title: Daily overtime limit & the 144-hour cap
items.text: Overtime is capped at 2 hours a day, and total working hours may not exceed 144 hours per 3-week period — paid at a minimum +25% premium, rising to at least +50% between 22:00 and 04:00 (Art. 19).

items.title: Meeting WPS payroll deadlines
items.text: Onshore private-sector wages must be paid electronically through the Wage Protection System (WPS) — employers who miss the 15-day payment window risk a freeze on new work permits (Ministerial Resolution No. 340 of 2026, in force since 1 June 2026).

items.title: Keeping biometric time tracking PDPL-compliant
items.text: The PDPL (Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021) explicitly classifies biometric data as sensitive personal data — cross-border transfers are tightly regulated.

rulesCalendar.title: A calendar that keeps pace with the moon
rulesCalendar.text: In the United Arab Emirates, all official public holidays are decreed centrally by the UAE Cabinet — uniformly for all seven emirates, with no cantonal or municipal variation like in Europe. The real challenge lies elsewhere: holidays whose exact date is only confirmed at short notice, and businesses that plan across several Gulf states.

items.title: Uniform nationwide, confirmed at short notice
items.text: Every holiday applies equally across all emirates — but religious dates such as Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha are confirmed only by a national moon-sighting committee, often just days in advance. New dates can be added to Klacks the moment they're announced.

items.title: Mix calendars
items.text: A Dubai business with branches in Saudi Arabia, Qatar or Oman needs several country calendars running at once — moon sightings occasionally differ by a day between Gulf states, and national days fall on different dates to begin with.

items.title: Binding or purely informational
items.text: For each calendar, you decide whether a holiday affects hours & premiums — or simply appears as a reminder.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off UAE businesses
solutions.subtitle: From automatic Ramadan hours to WPS-ready payroll security — everything works together.

items.title: Ramadan target hours can be set for everyone
items.text: Klacks can be set up with daily target hours reduced by 2 hours for all staff during the holy month of Ramadan — with no need to manually adjust every single schedule.

items.title: Overtime daily limit & 144-hour cap monitored live
items.text: Klacks warns before a shift is assigned if the 2-hour daily limit would be exceeded, and monitors total working hours per 3-week period live against the 144-hour cap; the night-work premium is calculated automatically, with an exactly configurable time window (22:00 to 04:00). On request, Klacks enforces such violations as a hard block: in block mode, a new violation can only be saved with documented supervisor approval (configurable per rule type).

items.title: The hour basis for WPS payroll
items.text: Klacks keeps hour accounts reconciled against the schedule that provide the hour basis for WPS payroll under Ministerial Resolution No. 340 of 2026 — documented on time, instead of risky guesswork.

items.title: PDPL-compliant on-premise hosting
items.text: Your scheduling and staff data stay on-premise, on your own infrastructure — with none of the cross-border data transfer that the PDPL tightly regulates for sensitive personal data.

items.title: Klacksy: rule-based, not a black box
items.text: The built-in AI assistant Klacksy schedules by voice command — traceable to defined skills and rules, never an opaque AI decision.

items.title: Absences covered fast
items.text: If someone calls in sick, Klacks immediately shows who is qualified and available — without tearing up the whole schedule.

klacksy.title: Klacksy: the assistant built into your team's workflow
klacksy.text: Klacksy isn’t a bolted-on marketing chatbot, but embedded directly in the Klacks interface. Staff and schedulers ask about shift times via chat, request shift swaps, or check availability. A built-in skills and rules system ensures Klacksy only ever makes traceable suggestions — never a black-box decision. For businesses with strict PDPL requirements around sensitive personal data, the AI model can also be hosted locally.
